section: Science · Ch44 — Universe, Solar System & Environment
subject: Science
stem: Which planet in our solar system is known as the 'Red Planet' due to iron oxide on its surface?
explanation: Mars appears reddish due to iron oxide (rust) covering much of its surface. Venus is the hottest planet (thick CO₂ atmosphere); Jupiter is the largest; Mercury is closest to the Sun.

section: Science · Ch44 — Universe, Solar System & Environment
subject: Science
stem: Day and night occur on Earth mainly because of the Earth's:
explanation: Earth's rotation on its own axis (once every ~24 hours) causes day and night as different parts face or turn away from the Sun. Revolution around the Sun (once a year) causes seasons, not day-night.

section: Science · Ch44 — Universe, Solar System & Environment
subject: Science
stem: The layer of the atmosphere that absorbs most of the Sun's harmful ultraviolet radiation, protecting life on Earth, is the:
explanation: The ozone layer, within the stratosphere, absorbs most harmful UV-B and UV-C radiation. The troposphere is the lowest layer where weather occurs; the ionosphere reflects radio waves; the exosphere is the outermost, thinnest layer.

subject: Science
stem: A child suffering from night blindness is most likely deficient in which vitamin?
explanation: Vitamin A deficiency causes night blindness (and, if severe, xerophthalmia). Vitamin C deficiency causes scurvy; Vitamin D deficiency causes rickets; B12 deficiency causes pernicious anaemia.

subject: Science
stem: Rickets, a disease causing soft and weak bones in children, is chiefly caused by deficiency of:
explanation: Rickets results from Vitamin D (and consequently calcium) deficiency, impairing bone mineralisation. Iron deficiency causes anaemia; iodine deficiency causes goitre.
